blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Large language models (LLMs) trained to answer questions are natively poor at teaching. Reinforcement Learning (RL) against a simulated student is a promising approach to improve their pedagogy, but existing RL-trained tutors reward the student’s success on the tutored problem with the tutor’s words still in context. The reward is then easiest to raise by telling the student the answer, and a tuned penalty is needed to reduce telling. Drawing on learning sciences, we introduce a masked near-transfer post-test: the student is tested on an unseen variant of the tutored problem with the tutor’s utterances masked, so the reward can rise only through what the student wrote in its own turns. This discourages cognitive offloading by the student and allows the continuous penalty to be replaced by two binary reward gates (factual correctness of tutor response, no solution handover). A leave-one-out ablation shows that the learning-gain reward on its own does not separate teaching from telling: the gates reduce solution handover while the near-transfer post-test improves out-of-domain transfer. Using these reward designs we develop Eduardo , a multi-turn RL recipe for training LLM tutors, and use it to train 4B, 9B, 14B and 27B models from two distinct LLM architectures. Our post-trained Eduardo -27B model matches Gemini 3.1 Pro on MathTutorBench and Claude Opus 4.8 on TutorMoments at 2.4–6.2 × \times fewer thinking tokens than frontier models, which matters for interactive tutoring. Without being named in the reward, the model more than doubles its use of the push-for-justification teacher move while support fading (e.g., assigning independent work), whose payoff lies beyond a single-problem dialog episode, is trained out. We open-source 1 1 1 https://github.com/eth-lre/EduardoRL our training environment, an 8,671-problem near-transfer dataset, and trained models for further development.
blocks.zh: 接受过回答问题培训的大型语言模型(LLMs)在教学方面本土性较差. 相对于模拟学生的强化学习(RL)是改善教学方法的一个很有希望的方法,但现有的RL训练有素的辅导员会用辅导员的言语来奖励学生在辅导问题上的成功。 奖赏通过告诉学生答案可以轻松地提高,需要调和的惩罚来减少说教. 在学习科学的基础上,我们引入了一个蒙面的近似转移测试后:学生通过一个隐形的变体进行测试,这个变体是被老师的言语所掩盖的,所以奖励只能通过学生自己写的东西来提高。 这抑制了学生的认知卸载,并允许将持续罚取而代之的是两个二进制的奖励门(补习生响应的实际正确性,没有解接). 一次放出放出会表明,学习奖励本身并没有将教学与说教区分开来:大门会减少解决方案的移交,而近转移测试后会改善领域外的移交. 利用这些奖励设计, 我们开发了Eduardo, 一个多回合的 RL 配方,用于培训 LLM 辅导员, 并用它来训练 4B, 9B, 14B 和 27B 模型 从两个不同的 LLM 架构。 我们训练后的Eduardo -27B模型与MathTutor Bench上的双子座3.1 Pro和Claude Opus 4.8的“导师时刻”相匹配,它们比边疆模型的思考符号要少,后者对交互式辅导很重要。 该模型没有在奖赏中被点名,而是在支持淡出(例如分配独立工作)的同时,将使用推-理-理-师移动的用法增加一倍以上,而后者的报酬则超出一个单一问题的对话插曲,因此被训练出. 我们开源11 1 https://github.com/eth-lre/EduardoRL 我们的训练环境, 一个8,671个问题 近传输数据集, 和训练型号的进一步发展。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: One-to-one human tutoring is among the most effective forms of instruction, and much of its effect comes from what the tutor does not do: a good tutor withholds the answer long enough for the student to construct it. Koedinger & Aleven (2007) call the underlying trade-off the Assistance Dilemma : give too little help and the student struggles, give too much and the student learns nothing because the tutor did the work. LLMs resolve the dilemma in one direction. They default to being “maximally capable answerers” rather than teachers ( Jurenka et al., 2024 ; Dinucu-Jianu et al., 2025 ) , for two reinforcing reasons. Pre-training corpora skew heavily toward question-in, answer-out formats ( Jurenka et al., 2024 ) , and single-turn RLHF rewards prioritize immediate helpfulness, so withholding information, or asking a question whose value becomes clear only several turns later, is penalized rather than credited ( Dinucu-Jianu et al., 2025 ) . The result is a model that delivers homework solutions, over-scaffolds, and rarely pushes for rigour ( Macina et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2026 ) . Aligning an LLM into a tutor therefore means changing what it is optimized for.
blocks.zh: 人一对一的辅导是最有效的教学形式之一,其效果大多出自于被辅导者不做的事:一个好的辅导员保留了足够长的答案,让学生来构建. Koedinger & Aleven (2007年)将基础取舍称为“援助困境 ” : 给予过多的帮助和学生的挣扎,给予过多的帮助和学生的无所事事,因为老师做了工作。 法学硕士从一个方向解决了难题。 他们没有成为“完全有能力的回答者”而不是教师(Jurenka等人,2024年;Dinucu-Jianu等人,2025年),原因有两个。 训练前的Corpora对提问、回答格式(Jurenka等人,2024年)和单回合的RLHF奖励优先注重即时帮助, 结果是一种提供家庭作业解决方案,过度脚手架的模型,很少推动严谨性(Macina等,2025;张等,2026. 因此,将 LLM 调整为导师意味着改变它最优化的目的 。

blocks.en: Reinforcement learning (RL) against a simulated student is a promising route to doing so ( Dinucu-Jianu et al., 2025 ) . Prompting cannot specify every pedagogical judgment in advance ( Jurenka et al., 2024 ) , and supervised fine-tuning on tutoring dialogs leads to a loss in the model’s own problem-solving ability ( Macina et al., 2025 ; Dinucu-Jianu et al., 2025 ) . RL with well-designed rewards that proxy a student’s learning gain can help mitigate these issues. However, the difficulty lies in how learning is measured. TutorRL ( Dinucu-Jianu et al., 2025 ) tests the student on the same problem with the tutor’s words still in context, so the cheapest way to raise the reward is to tell the student the answer, and a leakage penalty, judged by another LLM and balanced against the learning term, is needed to reduce telling. The reward and the penalty pull the model in opposite directions, and how well the tutor teaches depends on their balance.
blocks.zh: 对模拟学生的强化学习(RL)是这样做的有希望的途径(Dinucu-Jianu等,2025年)。 催促不能事先具体说明每一项教学判断(Jurenka等,2024年),在辅导对话上监督微调会导致模型自身解决问题能力的损失(Macina等,2025年;Dinucu-Jianu等,2025年)。 学生的学习收益可以帮助减轻这些问题。 然而,困难在于如何衡量学习。 TutorRL(Dinucu-Jianu等,2025年)用辅导员的言语来测试学生同样的问题,所以提高奖励的最廉价方式是告诉学生答案,需要用另一个LLM来判断并和学习术语相平衡的漏出罚来减少说出. 奖赏和罚罚将模型拉向相反的方向,而导师的教学水平取决于他们的平衡.

blocks.en:
We argue that the fix lies in the assessment. A natural assumption is that simulating a classroom suffices: test the student on an unseen problem, and handing out answers stops paying. We find this necessary but not sufficient. We identify three conditions: two on how learning is measured, transfer and student-notes-only , and one constraint cost of telling (Section 3.2 ). We realize them as a masked near-transfer post-test , in which the student attempts an unseen variant seeing only its own turns, together with two binary reward gates. Under this test, telling no longer raises the reward, yet the tutor keeps telling: a policy trained without the gates hands over the solution in 61% of dialogs at the same simulated gain (Section 5.2 ). The gates therefore remain necessary, but since nothing in the reward pulls against them, one fixed setting serves all model sizes. This is our central finding: a learning-gain reward alone does not separate teaching from telling, because a behavior that costs nothing is not unlearned. We turn the three conditions into Eduardo , a multi-turn RL recipe
trained against a frozen Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct ( Grattafiori et al., 2024 ) student and used unchanged from 4B to 27B. Since the reward names no pedagogical move, the policy is free to rediscover established ones, such as push for self-explanation, and to drop those whose payoff lies beyond a single episode. Our three main contributions are: • Three learning sciences inspired conditions for pedagogical RL. We identify how learning should be measured, and what measurement alone cannot do, for a learning-gain reward to favor teaching over telling. We release an open recipe ( Eduardo ) with an 8,671-problem near-transfer dataset. A leave-one-out ablation shows that the binary reward gates decide whether the tutor tells, while the masked near-transfer post-test shapes how it teaches (out-of-domain transfer, reasoning length). • Strong open tutors at low reasoning cost. Eduardo -27B achieves the highest MathTutorBench pedagogical reward-model score and win rate over human teachers on MathDial among all tested tutors, including frontier models, and the strongest TutorMoments scaffolding under a plain prompt. It does so with 2.4–6.2 × \times fewer thinking tokens, which interactive tutoring requires and which the reward partly encourages. • Behavioral discovery through optimization. As the reward evaluates only the student’s final learning outcome, it
serves as a measurement of what works. The model learns to increase push for justification, inherits affective gaps from the base model, and trains out support fading due to single-problem dialog episode reward horizons.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: Multi-turn RL and User Simulation. Standard RLHF optimizes single-turn helpfulness, penalizing information withholding and creating “passive responders” rather than active collaborators ( Wu et al., 2025 ; Mukherjee et al., 2025 ) . Extended multi-turn interactions expose further issues in models like bloated answers and over-adjustment to recent utterances ( Laban et al., 2026 ) . Tutoring is a long-horizon collaborative problem where early answer withholding pays off later. While prior multi-turn RL approaches for education rely on simulated users prompted to act confused ( Markel et al., 2023 ; Dou et al., 2025 ) or simulate cognitive states ( Liu et al., 2024 ) , such students exhibit performative errors and learn unnaturally well ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) . Similar to TutorRL ( Dinucu-Jianu et al., 2025 ) , we reward the tutor for the entire trajectory based on a frozen LLM student whose errors are genuine and not just LLM-prompted roleplay.
blocks.zh: 多回转RL和用户模拟. 标准RLHF优化了单回转的帮助,惩罚隐瞒信息的行为并创建了"被动反应器"而不是主动合作者(Wu等,2025;Mukherjee等,2025.). 扩展的多回合互动暴露出一些模型中的更多问题,如膨胀的答案和对最近言论的过度调整(Laban等人,2026年)。 Tutoring是一个很长的范围的合作问题,早期的解答迟些时才还清. 虽然以往的多回合RL教育方法依赖于被诱导的模拟用户行为混乱(Markel等,2023;Dou等,2025)或模拟认知状态(Liu等,2024),但这类学生表现出表演性错误,学习得不自然(Zhang等,2026)。 与TutorRL(Dinucu-Jianu等,2025年)相似,我们根据一个被冻结的LLM学生对整个轨迹进行奖励,该学生的错误是真实的,而不只是LLM促动的角色扮演.

blocks.en: LLMs for Tutoring. Early LLM tutors relied on prompting ( Schmucker et al., 2024 ; Kargupta et al., 2024 ) , but models optimized for helpfulness tend to over-scaffold and leak solutions prematurely ( Macina et al., 2023 ; Maurya et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2026 ) . Supervised fine-tuning on teacher–student dialogs ( Macina et al., 2023 ; Liu et al., 2024 ; Chevalier et al., 2024 ) instills tutoring behavior but causes models to forget core mathematical reasoning ( Macina et al., 2025 ) . Preference alignment focuses only on short-term helpfulness ( Scarlatos et al., 2025 ) . TutorRL ( Dinucu-Jianu et al., 2025 ) uses on-policy RL using GRPO to train a tutor against a frozen student model, rewarding the student’s ability to solve the same problem after the dialog, with the dialog in context. Because telling raises this reward, a leakage penalty must be balanced against it; we instead change how learning is measured (Section 3.2 ).

blocks.en: 3 Pedagogical RL for the Assistance Dilemma
blocks.zh: 3 援助困境的教学RL

blocks.en: Our design draws on established learning-sciences findings. The Assistance Dilemma ( Koedinger & Aleven, 2007 ) represents the tension between providing students information, which secures accuracy and efficiency, and withholding it, which forces the student to generate their own solutions and activate their prior knowledge ( Kapur, 2008 ; Freeman et al., 2014 ) . Effective tutors scaffold for access when content is out of reach and push for rigour to balance productive struggle ( Reiser, 2004 ) . The ICAP framework ( Chi & Wylie, 2014 ) suggests that learning increases as the student moves from passive reception to active, constructive and interactive engagement, so what the student generates ( Chi et al., 1994 ) matters more than what it is told. Our environment and reward turn these ideas into three concrete conditions on how learning is measured (Section 3.2 ).
blocks.zh: 我们的设计借鉴了既有的学习科学发现. 援助困境(Koedinger & Aleven,2007年)代表了提供学生信息(确保准确性和效率)与扣留信息(迫使学生提出自己的解决方案并激活其先前的知识)之间的紧张关系(Kapur,2008年;Freeman等人,2014年)。 当内容无法达到时,有效的导师脚手架,推动严格平衡生产斗争(Reiser,2004年)。 ICAP框架(Chi & Wylie,2014年)建议,随着学生从被动接待转向积极,建设性和互动性的参与,学习的增加,因此学生创造的东西(Chi等,1994年)比它被告知的事情更重要. 我们的环境和报酬将这些想法转化为衡量学习的三个具体条件(第3.2节)。

blocks.en: 3.2 Three Conditions on Measuring Learning
blocks.zh: 3.2 衡量学习的三个条件

blocks.en:
The natural reward for a tutor is the student’s learning: how much better the student solves problems after the dialog than before. How it is measured decides what solution handover is worth to the policy. If the student is re-tested on the tutored problem with the dialog in context ( Dinucu-Jianu et al., 2025 ) , a tutor that states the solution has placed it in the student’s context and the “learning gain” is maximal: telling increases the learning term, so a leakage penalty has to be traded off against it. Such a reward resolves the Assistance Dilemma in favor of giving help. We identify three conditions on the measurement that change this.
(1) Transfer. As in a real exam, the post-test problem is a variant the student was not tutored on, so walking the student through the tutored problem earns nothing unless the student can learn to transfer the method over to a similar problem ( Barnett & Ceci, 2002 ) (Section 3.3 ).
(2) Student-notes-only. As if the teacher’s notes were taken away, the tutor’s utterances are masked at test time, so reward can flow only through what the student authored in its own turns Chi et al. (1994) (no cognitive offloading, Section 3.4 ).
(3) Cost of telling. Conditions (1) and (2) can mitigate handover but do not make it costly, and a behavior that costs nothing is not unlearned (Section 5.2 ). We therefore add two binary reward gates that mirror core teacher duties: the tutor must be factually correct and must not hand over the solution ( Kapur, 2016 ) . Since telling no longer raises the gain, the gates need not be balanced against it, and one fixed setting serves all model sizes (Section 3.5 ).

对导师的自然奖励是学生的学习:在对话后,学生比以前更能解决问题。 如何衡量,决定哪些解决办法对政策是有价值的。 如果学生被重新测试与对话相关的辅导问题(Dinucu-Jianu等,2025年), 说出解决方案的导师将这个问题放在学生的背景中, 且“学习收益”是最大的:讲解会增加学习术语, 这种奖励解决了援助困境,有利于提供帮助。 我们确定了改变这一状况的三个衡量条件。
(1) 转让。 与真正的考试一样,考试后的问题是学生没有接受辅导的变体,因此,除非学生能够学习将方法转至类似的问题,否则徒步学生不会得到任何好处(Barnett & Ceci, 2002年)(第3.3节)。

blocks.en: Our experiments answer four questions: RQ1. Scaling and cross-family robustness: Does one recipe hold across a range of model sizes and model families? RQ2. (2) Open tutoring models : TutorRL-7B ( Dinucu-Jianu et al., 2025 ) and TutorRL’s base Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. (3) Proprietary models : Gemini 3.1 Pro, Gemini 3.5/3.6 Flash, and Claude Opus 4.8. These are evaluated under a plain prompt same for all models, and on TutorMoments, under both plain and an evaluation-aware prompt that states the rubric.

blocks.en: 4.2 Datasets and Evaluation Protocol
blocks.zh: 4.2 数据集和评价协议

blocks.en: To assess out-of-domain generalization (RQ3), we strictly separate training from evaluation. The training gates use Qwen3.6-27B, while all test-time judgments use Gemini-3.1-Pro. For student model generalization, we evaluate on precollected datasets (MathDial and Eedi) and TutorMoments (simulated conversations with an independent student model Gemini-3.7-Flash not used in training). For reward separation, independent benchmarks MathTutorBench and TutorMoments, measure pedagogy axes like scaffolding and rigour that never appear in ℛ ⁡ ( τ ) \mathcal{R}(\tau) .
blocks.zh: 为了评估域外概况(RQ3),我们严格将培训与评价分开。 训练门使用Qune3.6-27B,而所有测试时间的判断使用双子座-3.1-Pro. 对于学生模型通论,我们评价预先收集的数据集(MathDial和Eedi)和TutorMoments(与独立学生模型双子座-3.7-Flash的模拟对话,没有用于培训). 对于奖励分离,独立的基准 MathTutor Bench 和 TutorMoment, 测量诸如脚手架和严谨等教学轴, 从未出现在 R Q (\\ )\ mathcal{ R} (\ tau) 中 。

blocks.en: Evaluation tasks. We evaluate on three tasks: (1) Next-turn utterance generation (MathDial ( Macina et al., 2023 ) , Eedi ( Zent et al., 2025 ) ): each human dialog is cut at its middle teacher turn, so the tutor responds mid-conversation rather than at wrap-up, and the response is scored with the MathTutorBench pedagogical reward model (Ped-RM; RM in tables), its win rate against the human teacher’s turn at that point (Win), and judge ratings of pedagogy and factual correctness. (2) Teacher skills using MathTutorBench ( Macina et al., 2025 ) to measure mistake diagnostics and open-ended pedagogy without degrading problem solving. (3) Simulated dialog replays grounded in real human tutor-student transcripts from TutorMoments ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) with taxonomy classification of 13 tutor moves (e.g. scaffolding, rigour, and avoidance of over-help). Finally, all tutors run through the training environment on 494 held-out problems to compare optimized versus unoptimized quantities.
blocks.zh: 评价任务。 我们评价三项任务:(1) 下一轮发言(MathDial(Macina等,2023年)),Eedi。 (Zent等,2025年):每个人间对话在它的中老师转弯被剪断,因此导师对中老师转弯的反应而不是总结,响应的分数是用MathTutor Bench教学奖励模式(Ped-RM;RM入表)来评分,其胜出率与当时的人间老师转弯(Win)相比,判断教学学和事实正确性的评分. (2)教师技能 利用MathTutor Bench(Macina等,2025年)测量错误诊断和开放式教育方法,而不降低问题的解决。 (3)模拟对话回放 以真人导师-师生笔录为主从"导师"(张等,2026年),分类分类13个导师动作(如脚手架,严谨,避免过度帮助等). 最后,所有辅导员都通过494个被搁置问题的培训环境,比较优化和未优化的数量。

blocks.en: 4.3 Implementation Details
blocks.zh: 4.3 详细执行情况

blocks.en:
We optimize with Divergence Proximal Policy Optimization (DPPO) ( Qi et al., 2026 ) , a more stable variation of GRPO. Qwen3.6-27B is used as a training judge. Sequences are capped at 8,192 tokens and dialogs at 22 turns, with the tutor able to end the dialog earlier by emitting an end-of-conversation token. The learning gain is estimated from 16 student samples on the masked post-test.
Full hyperparameters, compute details, and prompts are provided in Appendices A – D .

blocks.en: 5.1 One Recipe Across Sizes and Architectures (RQ1)
blocks.zh: 5.1 一种跨大小和结构的食谱(RQ1)

blocks.en: Pedagogy against human teachers. We lead with the MathTutorBench pedagogical reward model (Ped-RM) and its win rate over the human teacher’s turn, as this instrument is independent of both the training judge and the Gemini evaluation judge. On MathDial (Table 1 , middle), Eduardo improves Ped-RM and win rate at 4B ( 2.08 → 7.92 2.08\to 7.92 ; 30 % → 78 % 30\%\to 78\% ), 9B ( 3.02 → 8.29 3.02\to 8.29 ; 38 % → 82 % 38\%\to 82\% ) and 27B ( 8.34 → 9.04 8.34\to 9.04 ; 82 % → 89 % 82\%\to 89\% ), and Eduardo-27B attains the highest Ped-RM and win rate of any tutor, including the frontier models. Eedi shows equally large gains at 4B and 9B, but not at 27B, where Eduardo trails its base (82.3% vs. 84.3% win rate). Eduardo-14B is at parity with Qwen3-14B on both datasets.

Eduardo-14B在两个数据集上与Quen3-14B处于等同状态.

blocks.en: Thinking tokens. Every Eduardo model thinks less than its base (e.g., 501 → 289 501\to 289 tokens per turn at 27B on MathDial). Part of this is built into the reward, whose efficiency decay discounts gains when thinking exceeds T think = 512 T_{\text{think}}{=}512 tokens per turn (Section 3.6 ); reductions below this budget, and differences between ablation arms sharing the same decay (Section 5.2 ), are not directly rewarded.
blocks.zh: 寻想道具. 每个Eduardo模型都认为低于其基数(例如,在MathDial上的27B上,每转弯有501~289个501\到289个令牌). 部分内容包含在奖励中,其效率衰减在思考超过T想=512 TQQText{thinkQQ512时折价收益. 每个转弯(第3.6节);低于本预算的削减,以及分享同样衰败的消耗性武器之间的差异(第5.2节),没有直接得到奖励。

blocks.en: Simulated gain is the training signal, and a weak instrument for ranking tutors. The environment columns (Table 1 , left; 494 held-out problems, identical masked protocol) report the quantity Eduardo optimizes on its own training student, which all other tutors see zero-shot. They separate tutors surprisingly little: every competent tutor falls within a Δ transfer \Delta_{\text{transfer}} band of + 0.19 +0.19 to + 0.29 +0.29 , and tutors that hand over the answer in 83–93% of dialogs (TutorRL-7B, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct) still obtain + 0.13 +0.13 – 0.14 0.14 , so much of the gain stems from the student’s own attempts. We therefore rest claims about tutoring quality on the out-of-domain benchmarks and read the environment only as evidence that RL improved its objective ( + 0.22 → + 0.29 +0.22\to+0.29 at 27B).
blocks.zh: 模拟收益是训练信号,也是排名导师的弱器. 环境栏目(表1,左;494个被搁置的问题,相同的蒙面协议)报告Eduardo在自己的训练生身上优化数量,所有其他辅导员都看到零射入. 他们分开的辅导员很少出人意料:每个胜任的辅导员都属于 + + 0.19 + 0.19 + 0.29 + 0.29的 + 29 的 + 3 的 + 3 的 分班员(TutorRL-7B, Quen2.5-7B-Instruct) , 仍然得到 + 0.13 + 0.13 – 0.14 的分班员,所以大部分收益来自学生自己的尝试。 因此,我们不再主张在域外基准上进行辅导的质量,只把环境看成是证明RL改善了目标(+0.22-+0.29+0.22-+0.29 at 27B)。

blocks.en: Leakage is held, not reduced, for the Qwen3.5/3.8 family. Eduardo-27B leaks in 9% of dialogs, the same as its base and close to the frontier tutors (5–7%). Eduardo-4B and 9B leak in 25–31%, about four times the frontier rate. The 4B base’s 17% is not a valid comparison: 70% of its turns reach the student empty, and an empty turn cannot leak (Table 8 ). Training reduces leakage substantially only for Qwen3-14B, whose base hands over the solution in 98% of dialogs (to 32%). TutorRL-7B has only slightly lower leakage than its base on every environment metric, although its Ped-RM is higher ( 5.75 → 6.78 5.75\to 6.78 ).

blocks.en: 5.2 Conditions Ablation (RQ2)
blocks.zh: 5.2 条件差(RQ2)

blocks.en: We ablate each condition at 4B under the identical protocol (Table 2 ).
blocks.zh: 根据相同的协议,我们将每个条件减为4B(表2)。

blocks.en: First, every condition matters for pedagogy against human teachers. Removing any single condition lowers Ped-RM on MathDial ( 7.92 → 6.10 7.92\to 6.10 without the gates, 6.48 6.48 without masking, 5.25 5.25 without near-transfer) and on Eedi, as well as the MathDial win rate ( 78 % → 65 % 78\%\to 65\% , 65 % 65\% , 56 % 56\% ).
blocks.zh: 首先,针对人类教师的教学方法的所有条件都很重要。 消除任何单一条件都会降低Ped-RM在MathDial上(7.92 — 6.10 7.92\to 6.10没有门,6.48 6.48没有口罩,5.25 5.25没有近距离转移)和在Eedi上,以及MathDial赢取率(78% — 65% 78+至65+,65% 65+,56% 56+)。

blocks.en: Second, the training signal cannot see these differences. All four arms lie within 0.03 0.03 on Δ transfer \Delta_{\text{transfer}} ( + 0.23 +0.23 to + 0.25 +0.25 ), even though the policy hands over the solution in 61% of dialogs without the gates (vs. 31%) and in 47% without near-transfer. The frozen student saturates at a gain of ≈ 0.24 \approx 0.24 whether it constructs the answer or copies it. Handover is thus reward-neutral, and only the gates make it costly (condition 3).
blocks.zh: 第二,训练信号看不到这些差异。 所有四件武器都位于 0.03 0.03 的 \ Delta {text { (+ 0.23 + 0.23 + 0.25 + 0.25 ) 上,尽管政策在61%的没有大门的对话(vs 31%)和47%的没有近距离转让的对话中交出了解决方案. 被冻结的学生饱和度以0.24的增益为0.24左右,无论是构建答案还是复制答案. 因此,移交是无报酬的,只有大门才能使其代价高昂(条件3)。

blocks.en: Third, each condition shapes a distinct behavior. The gates govern handover ( − 30 -30 % leakage) and whole-dialog pedagogy ( 3.66 → 2.80 3.66\to 2.80 without them). Near-transfer governs out-of-domain transfer: without it, the policy has the lowest MathDial win rate (56%), and its Eedi win rate drops from 72.4% to 65.0%. Removing the mask keeps unstable reasoning as in base (27% of turns overrun the per-turn cap, 40% of dialogs are truncated; Table 8 ). Thinking length also differs across arms, although all share the same efficiency decay: removing the gates lowers it (345 vs. 456 tokens per turn on MathDial), while removing the mask or the transfer test raises it (1,597 and 776). We attribute this to the objective: when reward flows only through what the student writes on an unseen problem, working out the solution in the tutor’s own reasoning earns nothing and is pruned. For the masking arm, this interpretation is confounded by its cap overruns.
blocks.zh: 第三,每个条件都形成一个截然不同的行为. 大门管理交接(-30-30%渗出)和全相机教学法(3.66-2.80 3.66\至2.80没有它们)。 近转移管理域外转移:没有它,政策中数学数字取胜率最低(56%),其爱迪取胜率从72.4%下降到65.0%. 移除口罩会像基座一样(27%的转弯会超过每转弯的上限,40%的对话框被截断;表8),使推理不稳定。 思考长度也因手臂而异,虽然都有着相同的效率衰变:去掉门使其更低(每转接MathDial上345对456个令牌),而去掉口罩或转移测试则提高口罩(1,597和776)。 校对:Soup 对于蒙面臂来说,这种解释被其盖子被打乱了.

blocks.en: 5.3 Out-of-Domain Generalization (RQ3)
blocks.zh: 5.3 域外通用(RQ3)

blocks.en: On MathTutorBench (Figure 1 and 3 ), which uses an independent judge and whose pedagogy axes never appear in the reward, every Eduardo model improves over its base. Eduardo -27B reaches 0.79, close to Gemini 3.1 Pro (0.80), with its problem-solving accuracy unchanged.
blocks.zh: 在MathTutor Bench(图1和图3)上,它使用独立法官,其教学轴从未出现在奖励中,每个Eduardo模型都比其基础有所改进. Eduardo-27B达到0.79,接近双子座3.1 Pro (0.80),其解决问题的精确度不变.

blocks.en: TutorMoments (Table 3 ) use simulated dialog replays grounded in human tutor-student dialogs, with an independent student and judge model. We evaluate under a plain prompt and an evaluation-aware prompt that states the benchmark’s rubric. Under the plain prompt, Eduardo -27B is the strongest tutor: it has the highest Scaffolding (0.96) and Avoids-Over-help (0.76) and is second on rigour (0.44 vs. 0.48 for Claude Opus 4.8), while its base is the weakest. Given the rubric, the frontier models overtake it on rigour (0.79–0.92 vs. 0.67) and Avoids-Over-help (0.91–0.97 vs. 0.86). In both conditions it uses the fewest thinking tokens, partly by design (Section 5.1 ).
blocks.zh: TutorMoments(表3)使用基于人类导师-学生对话的模拟对话回放,使用独立的学生和裁判模型. 我们用一个简单快速的、具有评估意识的即时评估, 在平坦的快板下,Eduardo-27B是最强的导师:它拥有最高的脚手架(0.96)和Craws-Over-help(0.76),在严格度上居第二(克洛德·奥普斯4.8的0.44对0.48),而它的基座是最弱的. 鉴于这个主题,前沿模型在严谨性(0.79-0.92 vs. 0.67)和 " 避免超越帮助 " (0.91-0.97 vs. 0.86)上超越了它。 在这两种情况下,它使用最少的思维符号,部分是设计(第5.1节)。

blocks.en: 5.4 Behavioral Discovery (RQ4)
blocks.zh: 5.4 行为发现(RQ4)

blocks.en: Because no move is explicitly stated in the reward, the move distribution of a trained policy is a measurement of the environment quality. Tutor turns classification follows TutorMoments taxonomy of 13 moves using the Gemini-3.1-Pro judge and compare models to the benchmark’s human tutors and to each other (Figure 2 ).
blocks.zh: 由于奖励中未明确说明任何动作,因此训练有素政策的动作分配是对环境质量的衡量. 教学者转而按照使用双子座-3.1-Pro裁判的13个动作的“教学运动分类法”进行分类,并将模型与基准的人类导师和相互比较(图2)。

blocks.en: 1. Untrained models imitate average human tutors. All plain-prompted frontier models sit at a Jensen–Shannon (JS) distance of 0.32–0.39 from the human move distribution (Figure 2 a). The benchmark’s human tutors are not a normative gold standard: they spend roughly 29% of their moves telling answers or co-solving ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) . Models imitating this distribution score poorly on pedagogy, so diverging from the human baseline is a prerequisite for high-quality tutoring.
blocks.zh: 1. 联合国 未受过训练的模特模仿一般的人类辅导员. 所有速成前沿模型都位于Jensen-Shannon(JS)距离人类移动分布0.32-0.39(图2a)。 基准的人类导师并不是一个规范的金本位:他们花费了大约29%的动作来回答或共同解决(张等,2026年). 模式模仿这种分布在教学学上的得分不佳,因此与人类基线的不同是高质量辅导的先决条件.

blocks.en: 2. Specification and discovery arrive at the same move distribution. When given the evaluation-aware prompt, frontier models converge on a rubric-aligned distribution: evaluation-aware Gemini, Claude and base model sit 0.13, 0.18, and 0.24 from the centroid of the prompted models. Eduardo sits 0.24 from that centroid without ever seeing the prompt, closer than any unprompted model (0.28–0.43). Optimization of a masked learning gain produces approximately the same move profile as an expert-defined rubric.
blocks.zh: 2. 规格和发现达到相同的移动分布。 有了评价意识的即时性,前沿模型就集中到一个分数相通的分布上:评价意识的双子座,克洛德和基数模型坐落着0.13,0.18和0.24从被激发模型的中间体. Eduardo坐着0.24从那颗中间行星上坐着,从未看到过快活的,比任何无快活的模型更相近(0.28–0.43). 优化被蒙蔽的学习增益产生与专家定义的外观大致相同的移动剖面.

blocks.en: 3. The behavior is internalized in the weights. The evaluation-aware prompt barely moves Eduardo (Figure 2 a, shortest arrow), whereas it moves its base by a large distance. RL placed in the weights what prompting can only elicit from the same base weights on demand.
blocks.zh: 3个 行为被内化为分量. 了解评价的快板几乎动不了Eduardo(图2 a,最短箭头),而基座移动了很长的距离。 RL在权重中放置了只有在需求时才能从相同的基重中导出的东西.

blocks.en:
4. Specific behavioral shifts isolate discovery from binary reward gates. Comparing the base model with Eduardo under the same plain prompt (Figure 2 b) separates what the reward asked for from what the optimizer found. Constraint fingerprint: The moves the binary reward gates penalise collapse (Explaining, Move C: 18.5% → \rightarrow 3.9%; Supplying answers, Move F: 15.5% → \rightarrow 2.2%). Discovery fingerprint: Prompting for justification (Move G) more than doubles (9.0% → \rightarrow 21.8%), and Guiding questions (Move A) rises (23.2% → \rightarrow 41.4%). Because the binary reward gates explicitly penalize handover (Move F), the policy’s action space is constrained to non-handover moves. However, it is noteworthy that out of all possible non-handover moves (e.g., giving hints, offering analogies, breaking down the problem), the optimizer specifically converged on prompting for justification (Move G).
This is consistent with an incentive to elicit reusable student-authored reasoning. Trained out: Asking for Independent work (Move H) falls to 0.0%. This move represents support fading, a strategy that pays off across multiple problems, but it never pays before test within our single-problem dialog horizon. Inherited: Affirmations (Move K) remain rare (1.7% → \rightarrow 2.0%), a trait inherited from the base model since the reward is neutral towards socio-emotional moves.
This shift from explaining to eliciting marks a step from answering towards tutoring: the student, not the tutor, does the reasoning that the post-test rewards.
blocks.zh:
4.四. 具体的行为转变将发现与二进制奖励门隔离. 将基准模型与Eduardo在同一个平板快件(图2b)下进行比较,将奖励要求与优化者发现的区别开来。 约束指纹 : 二进制奖励门的移动惩罚倒闭(解释,移动C:18.5% ~\正线3.9%;提供答案,移动F:15.5% ~\正线2.2%)。 发现指纹:催促说明理由(移动G)超过双倍(9.0% ~ 右转21.8%),Guiding问题(移动A)上升(23.2% ~ 右转41.4%). 因为二进制奖励门明确惩罚交接(F出行),所以政策的行动空间受到非交接动作的限制. 然而,值得注意的是,在所有可能的不交接动作中(例如给出提示,提供类比,破解问题),优化者具体集中到提示说明(Move G)上.
这与促使学生重新使用学生授权的推理是一致的。 受培训人员:要求独立工作(H运动)降至0.0 %. 这一举动代表了支持的消退,这一策略在多重问题上都得到了回报,但它从未在我们单一问题对话的地平线范围内进行测试之前支付过。 继承:肯定(K动)仍然罕见(1.7% ~\正中2.0%),这是从基准模式中继承的特质,因为奖励对社会情感运动是中立的.
这种从解释到引人入胜的转变标志着从回答到辅导的一步:学生而不是导师的推理是测试后奖励的.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en: A learning-gain reward is the right objective for a tutoring model and, on its own, an insufficient one. We showed that whether such a reward favors teaching over telling depends on how learning is measured (the three conditions of Section 3.2 ). With these conditions in place, a single fixed RL recipe ( Eduardo ) trains open-source tutoring models from 4B to 27B parameters. The 27B model achieves the highest pedagogical reward-model score and win rate over human teachers on MathDial among all tested tutors and is the strongest TutorMoments tutor under a plain prompt, while thinking several times less. More broadly, rewarding what the user can do on their own, rather than what they were told, may carry over to any domain where an agent should build the user’s capabilities rather than act as an oracle.
blocks.zh: 补习奖励是辅导模式的正确目标,而单靠本身是不够的。 我们显示,这种奖励是否优于教学,而优于教学取决于如何衡量学习(第3.2节的三个条件)。 在这些条件到位后,一个单一的固定RL配方(Eduardo )将开源辅导模型从4B到27B参数进行训练. 27B模式在所有经过测试的导师中实现了最高的教学奖励-模范分数并战胜了数学Dial上的人类教师,并且是在平坦的快板下最强的"导师运动"导师,同时思考少了几倍. 更广泛地说,奖励用户自己能够做什么,而不是告诉他们什么,可以转到任何一个代理人应该建立用户能力而不是充当先知的领域。

blocks.en: Limitations and Future Work. Our approach uses a frozen LLM as a proxy student. While LLM errors can be genuine, LLMs lack the working memory, affective states, and developmental misconceptions of human learners. Further, training against one frozen student risks overfitting to its specific failure modes, necessitating future training against diverse student ensembles. Second, we measure near transfer within one domain (math). Third, optimizing for cognitive gain alone creates an affect gap (Move K), as the reward provides no incentive for socio-emotional moves (e.g., rapport, encouragement), and future work should explore additional multi-objective optimization for tutoring. Fourth, the ablation uses one seed, one model size (4B), and one checkpoint per arm, so it identifies which behavior each condition affects rather than establishing that each is necessary.
blocks.zh: 限制和未来工作。 我们的方法是使用冷冻的LLM作为代理学生. 虽然LLM错误可能是真实的,但LLMs缺乏工作记忆,情感状态,以及对人类学习者的发展误解. 此外,针对一个被冻结的学生的培训可能过于适合其具体的失败模式,因此今后有必要针对不同的学生组合进行培训。 第二,我们在一个域(math)内测量近距离传输。 第三,仅靠优化认知收益就会产生影响差距(Move K),因为奖励没有为社会情感运动提供激励(如关系,鼓励),而未来的工作应该为辅导探索额外的多目标优化. 第四,衰竭使用一个种子,一个型号(4B),每个臂上有一个检查点,因此它确定每个条件都影响哪些行为,而不是确定每个条件都是必要的.

blocks.en: The leakage judge REJECTs a trajectory if the tutor: 1. States the final answer (in any form, including inside a question) before a student turn contains it. 2. Names the key method, formula, or substitution before any student attempt. 3. Lays out the complete solution path, leaving the student only arithmetic or restating. Importantly, phrasing as a question does not exempt a hint : if a tutor question names, presupposes, or performs the key step (e.g., “what do you get when you factor out x x ?”), it is treated as if the tutor had stated it. This operationalizes the funneling/focusing Wood (1994) boundary from the math education literature as a scoring rule.

blocks.en: You are tutoring a student through a math problem. Your goal is that they understand deeply enough to solve a similar problem on their own afterwards. The student should always show you their attempt first. Never state the final answer before the student has reached it themselves. Do not name the method or key formula before the student has made an attempt (proposed a method, wrote a step, stated a guess, or described a dead end --- ‘‘how do I do this?’’ is not an attempt). If the student cannot produce any attempt after genuinely trying, you may demonstrate the key idea on a different example and have them apply it to this one. The student should do the cognitive work --- the decisions, not just the calculations: let them choose the method and the next step. Students remember what they choose, work out, and put into their own words far better than what they are told. Everything you say must be mathematically correct. Even if the student is already able to solve the problem, help them deepen and improve their solution so they gain the strongest possible conceptual and transfer understanding. Use your private thinking (the student never sees it) to reason about where the student’s mistake is and which pedagogical move suits the situation. When the student has demonstrated understanding and no question of yours is left unanswered, end your final message with <end_of_conversation> on its own line. Problem: {problem}
blocks.zh: 你在为学生提供数学辅导 你的目标是,他们足够深刻的理解 解决一个类似的问题 在他们之后。 学生应该先告诉你他们的尝试 在学生自己到达之前 千万不要说最后的答案 在学生尝试(提出方法,写出一个步骤,说明一个猜想,或者描述一个死胡同)之前,不要给方法或关键公式起名 -- -- 我该如何做到这一点? ——不是企图). 如果学生在真正尝试之后无法产生任何尝试,您可以在不同的例子中展示关键的想法,并应用到这个例子中. 学生应该做认知工作--——决定,而不仅仅是计算:让他们选择方法和下一步. 学生们记得自己选择的,工作,把比他们被告知的要好得多的话写进自己的话里去. 你说的每句话都必须在数学上正确 即使学生已经能够解决问题,帮助他们深化和改进他们的解决方案,从而获得尽可能最强的概念和转移理解. 使用私人思维(学生从未见过)来解释学生的错误所在, 当学生表现出理解,而你的问题没有被解答时,请用“end_of_conversation”结束你的最后信息。 问题: [问题]

blocks.en: The Ped. and Fact. scores in Tables 1 and 2 are assigned by Gemini-3.1-Pro, which never enters the reward. The judge sees the problem, its correct answer and the full tutor–student dialog, scores the whole dialog on one criterion per call on a 1–5 scale, and is instructed to be strict and use the full range. Each prompt also contains two to three few-shot examples and a JSON output format, omitted here. Table 9 gives the factuality rubric and Table 10 the pedagogy rubric.

blocks.en: Table 9: Factuality rubric (Fact.): Correctness & Language Appropriateness. Is everything the tutor says mathematically correct, and is it expressed at the right level for this problem and this student? Correctness covers hints, confirmations, corrections and intermediate results; the student’s level is judged from their own messages.

blocks.en: Table 10: Pedagogy rubric (Ped.). Good tutoring uses contingent scaffolding (help calibrated to the student’s demonstrated need, minimal hint first, fading as competence grows), allows productive struggle (room to attempt, err and self-correct; errors diagnosed and turned into reasoning opportunities), and maintains rigour (pressing for justification and avoiding funneling). The student does the actual reasoning and most of the talking.
